# Logging and telemetry

<!-- Generated by `npm run train` from the sources each rule cites. To change a rule for good, change its source or say so in training/feedback.md; the next training run regenerates this file. -->

- **Never write a credential to a log message, audit event, span tag, metric tag or exception message. This covers access, refresh and ID tokens, session ids and handles, cookie values, OAuth `state`, authorization codes, continuation URLs or state, client secrets, bootstrap credentials, passwords and key material. Never generate a token or credential at startup and write it to the logs.** These values grant access, and logs, audit records and exported telemetry are read far more widely than the store that protects them. A logged JWT expires, can't be revoked on its own, and has to be scraped from the logs. *Check:* Look at the arguments of log calls, audit event properties, `Activity` tags and exception messages for variables holding tokens, codes, `state`, session ids, cookies, secrets, passwords or key bytes (wrapped or unwrapped). Pay most attention to seeding, startup, session and continuation code. Audit events about keys may name the provider, reference, identity, state and failure, but never the material. <sub>Identity ADR-1044; Identity ADR-1290; Identity ADR-1380; Identity ADR-1414; Identity docs/backend-for-frontend.md; Identity csharp.instructions.md; Identity outcomes of #504</sub>
- **When logging a request or a URL, log only the scheme, host, port and path (for example `uri.GetLeftPart(UriPartial.Path)`). Never log the query string, user information or fragment, and never log a resolved IP address of an outbound target.** Query strings carry codes, `id_token_hint` and capability tokens such as an RFC 9101 `request_uri`. A requester can force a fetch to fail and get those values copied into logs, where anyone who reads the logs can replay them. Resolved addresses expose internal topology. *Check:* Look for log arguments or exception messages that use `Request.QueryString`, `GetDisplayUrl()`, `Uri.AbsoluteUri`, `Uri.ToString()`, a raw URL string from a request or a registered endpoint, or an `IPAddress`. An exception that refuses an address should name only the host. <sub>Identity csharp.instructions.md; Identity outcomes of #825; Identity ADR-1315</sub>
- **Don't enable logging of request or response bodies, the query string or trailers through global `HttpLoggingOptions.LoggingFields` (including `HttpLoggingFields.All`) or through configuration, and never add a credential header such as `Authorization` or `Cookie` to the allow-listed headers. Log only request and response properties, allow-listed headers and duration. An endpoint that needs its body logged opts in by itself, in reviewed code.** Bodies, queries and credential headers carry secrets, codes, tokens, passwords and personal data. A configuration setting is an operator's dial, so protection that depends on configuration is no protection. *Check:* Look for `LoggingFields` that include `RequestBody`, `ResponseBody`, `RequestQuery`, `RequestTrailers`, `ResponseTrailers` or `All`, for configuration sections that turn on body logging, and for credential headers added to `RequestHeaders` or `ResponseHeaders`. *Note:* Route groups whose bodies carry credentials or personal data should be marked confidential so they can't opt in. <sub>Identity ADR-1503; Identity csharp-production.instructions.md</sub>
- **Don't use `[HttpLogging(...)]` or `.WithHttpLogging(...)` endpoint metadata to turn on body, query or credential-header logging.** The framework's metadata can turn on any field, the query string included, on any endpoint, including one that carries credentials, so it is not a safe way to opt in. *Check:* Look for `[HttpLogging(` attributes or `.WithHttpLogging(` calls in endpoint mapping code. <sub>Identity ADR-1503</sub>
- **Cap the `Microsoft.AspNetCore.Hosting.Diagnostics` log category at `Warning` with a filter rule that applies to every logging provider, so that a provider-scoped level such as `Logging:Console:LogLevel` can't raise it. If the cap isn't there, docs must not claim that no log level writes a query string.** At Information this logger writes `Request starting` and `Request finished` lines that contain the full URL and query string, outside HTTP logging. Guarding only the HTTP logging middleware still leaks `id_token_hint`, request objects and query-string tokens. *Check:* Look at logging configuration and `LoggerFilterOptions` code for this category raised to Information or lower, or capped for only one provider. Also look at changes that guard against query strings in logs but don't filter this category. A good test sends a GET with sentinel query values at Debug and asserts that no log record contains them. <sub>Identity ADR-1503; Identity outcomes of #785</sub>
- **On a named `HttpClient` whose request URIs may carry sensitive queries, remove `IHttpClientFactory`'s default logging handlers (for example with `RemoveAllLoggers()`) when another component already logs those requests.** The factory's default loggers write each request URI, query included. *Check:* Look at client registrations for forwarded, proxied or caller-supplied URIs and check whether the default logging is cleared. <sub>Identity ADR-1381</sub>
- **On paths that refuse a login, hit an attempt limit or fail after a commit, log the tenant, the limit, the window or partition name, and the subject id where it is verified. Never log the user name the request presented, the remote address, the client identifier or the reason. Key shared-state entries by a digest of the folded user name, not by the name itself.** Operators need to see the refusal without the logs or shared state disclosing who tried to sign in or from where. *Check:* Look for counter keys built from the raw user name, and for log calls on limit, refusal or post-commit failure paths whose parameters include a user name, IP address, client_id or reason. *Note:* ADR-1351 sets the levels: a failed post-commit session termination is logged at Error because sessions stay active, and a failed reset of the failed-attempt counter is logged at Warning because it fails closed. <sub>Identity ADR-1237; Identity ADR-1351; Identity ADR-1399</sub>
- **Record an audit event only once the change or disclosure is certain: after the commit succeeds, after the response is fully built (including signing or encryption), and only when this call actually changed state, for example when the revoked count is above zero. Record the event in the handler that knows the actor, not in the store or in a pipeline stage or enricher.** An event recorded earlier can audit a change that never happened, a disclosure whose response then failed, or a revocation that a concurrent request already made, which would then be audited twice. The store doesn't know who the actor is. *Check:* Look for audit calls placed before the save or commit, before JWT signing, encryption or response serialization, or inside persistence code or a claims enricher. Look for calls after a revocation that don't check the returned count or boolean. Look for a revocation or grant path that records no event, or records one without the subject whose grant ended. <sub>Identity ADR-1028; Identity ADR-1222; Identity ADR-1401; Identity ADR-1465</sub>
- **Don't also log, at the call site, an outcome that the code publishes as an audit or domain event. Log only the mechanics, such as lost races, failures and a failure to publish the event. Logging, metrics and tracing of the outcome are done by handlers that subscribe to the event.** Two streams then report the same fact under different templates and EventIds, and they drift apart. Inline logs written before the commit also record changes that a lost race later throws away. *Check:* Look for `ILogger` or `Log.*` calls describing a created, retired, removed or succeeded entity next to a `PublishAsync` or audit recorder call for the same fact, especially before the commit. <sub>Identity ADR-1047; Identity ADR-1404; Identity outcomes of #551; Identity outcomes of #702</sub>
- **Don't report a log entry beside a published event as duplication when it carries different information for a different reader. Two examples: an exception diagnostic for the operator behind an errored protocol response (unexpected `server_error` at Error, other errors at Debug), and a limit log that carries the partition, limit and window while the audit event carries the client, method and error code.** These logs complement the event, and no rule forbids logging next to a published event. *Check:* Compare the log's fields with the event's fields, and report only when they carry the same information. <sub>Identity ADR-1047; Identity outcomes of #547</sub>
- **Never use a tenant, client, subject, user, session or request identifier, an IP address, a hostname, `server.address`/`server.port`, a URL or path, or any free-form or caller-supplied value as a metric attribute. Put identifiers on logs, traces and audit records instead.** Every distinct attribute value creates a new metric series, so unbounded values grow with the customer base until the backend drops data. They also leak identifying data. Traces and logs pay nothing per series. *Check:* Look at the `TagList`/`KeyValuePair` tags passed to counters and histograms for ids, user names, addresses, hosts, ports, URLs, paths, messages or display names. *Note:* csharp-production.instructions.md also bans identifying values from span attributes, and docs/backend-for-frontend.md bans subjects and request paths from all telemetry. ADR-1197, docs/metrics.md and docs/audit-records.md, which are more specific, put tenant, client and subject on traces and logs. Secrets and personal data never go on spans. Per-tenant usage belongs in a durable store read through an API, not in metrics. <sub>Identity ADR-1197; Identity ADR-1199; Identity ADR-1283; Identity docs/audit-records.md; Identity docs/metrics.md; Identity docs/backend-for-frontend.md; Identity csharp.instructions.md; Identity csharp-production.instructions.md</sub>
- **Take every metric attribute value from a bounded vocabulary the server controls: constants, registered type names, enums, or OAuth error codes the server chose. Record an unknown or unregistered value as `_OTHER`. Never select behavior, metric attributes or audit fields from free-form operator text such as a display name.** Vocabularies are open and the backend's series budget is limited, so a caller must never be able to create a series with a value it chose. Free text can't safely select behavior either. *Check:* Look for tag values taken straight from request parameters, configuration, exception messages or echoed error values without being checked against a registered set with `_OTHER` as the fallback. Also look for branches or tags that read a free-form name setting. <sub>Identity ADR-1197; Identity ADR-1289; Identity docs/metrics.md; Identity csharp.instructions.md; Identity csharp-production.instructions.md</sub>
- **Use a named constant for a bounded attribute value such as `_OTHER` or `timeout`, preferably an existing shared one, rather than a bare string literal. Where the shared constant can't be referenced, define a local constant with a comment naming the constant it mirrors.** Bare literals let one metric drift from the shared vocabulary other metrics use. *Check:* Look for string literals used as metric tag values or `error.type` values where a shared constant exists. <sub>Identity outcomes of #529</sub>
- **Set `error.type` on a duration histogram or span only when the operation fails, and set it to the exception's full type name (`GetType().FullName`) or a fixed failure-reason constant.** This keeps the attribute bounded and in line with the OpenTelemetry semantic conventions that dashboards rely on. *Check:* Look for `error.type` set on success paths, or set to an exception message, `ToString()` or other free text. <sub>Identity docs/metrics.md; Identity ADR-1197</sub>
- **When a host collects `System.Net.Http` metrics, add a view that keeps only bounded attributes and drops `server.address` and `server.port`.** Those attributes name the hosts of client-registered or caller-supplied URIs, which makes them unbounded and identifying. *Check:* Where `AddMeter("System.Net.Http")` is added, check that a view filters the tag keys down to bounded ones. <sub>Identity docs/metrics.md</sub>
- **Give an audit failure a required, stable, machine-readable error code, using the OAuth error code where one applies. Keep human-readable text in the optional message, and don't add a free-text reason field. Give failures that need different fixes distinct codes, for example a certificate that fails trust validation versus a trusted certificate that doesn't match the registration.** Operators group, filter and pivot by code. Free text can't be filtered without parsing prose, and a merged reason hides whether the PKI configuration or the certificate is wrong. *Check:* Look for audit errors built without a code, codes derived from exception messages, custom codes where an OAuth code applies, string `Reason`/`Description` properties, or failure branches that share one code. <sub>Identity ADR-1283; Identity docs/audit-records.md; Identity ADR-1173</sub>
- **Put only a verified subject or client identifier in an audit record's subject id field. Record an unverified user name the request presented in a separate details member, such as `attempted_username`, and leave the subject id empty.** `subject_id` stays trustworthy only if it never holds unverified input. *Check:* On failure paths such as refused credentials, look for user names or ids from the request assigned to the subject id field. <sub>Identity docs/audit-records.md</sub>
- **Don't record a second audit event for a failure that another component already audits, such as a credential the authentication handler already recorded as a failed authentication.** The audit trail would count one failure twice. *Check:* In endpoint code after authentication, look for audit calls on the unauthenticated branch that repeat the handler's failure event. <sub>Identity ADR-1401</sub>
- **Audit OAuth/OpenID Connect protocol error responses once per errored request, from a single endpoint-level funnel, not by publishing an error event at each call site that produces an error.** Errors reach the response both through thrown exceptions and through returned error results. Publishing at each call site misses some paths and counts others twice. *Check:* Look for endpoint or handler code that publishes a protocol-error audit event directly instead of relying on the endpoint-level funnel. <sub>Identity ADR-1047</sub>
- **A bulk or composite operation that writes resources records, for each write, the same resource-change audit event that the resource's own endpoint records, plus one summary event for the whole operation. Don't ask a secondary write path to audit writes that the resource's own endpoints don't audit.** A resource's audit trail then looks the same whichever path changed it. Adding auditing to a resource is a change to its endpoints, not to the secondary path. *Check:* Compare the bulk or secondary path with the primary endpoint handler: does the handler take an audit recorder and record events for the same write? <sub>Identity ADR-1425; Identity outcomes of #592</sub>
- **Use the same field names in the audit record, the log state, the span tags and the metric attributes, declared once as constants rather than repeated as string literals.** An operator can then move between a record, its log entry, its trace and its metrics without translating names. Log state isn't checked by a source generator, so the constants are the only guard. *Check:* Look for audit keys written as inline literals, or for log, span or metric names that differ from the record's snake_case field names other than by their `audit.` or metric prefix. <sub>Identity ADR-1283; Identity docs/audit-records.md</sub>
- **Log a structured audit or event record as flattened key/value state, not as one serialized JSON string property or a sentence built from a template. Flatten one level of nested details only, emit arrays and deeper values as raw JSON text, omit null members, and keep numbers as numbers.** A collector can't index fields hidden inside an opaque string or inside prose. The limits bound how many index fields one event can create, and numbers stay queryable as numbers. *Check:* Look for audit logging that passes the serialized record as a single `{Record}` placeholder, and for flattening code that recurses into arrays or nested objects, emits keys for nulls, or turns numbers into strings. <sub>Identity ADR-1283; Identity docs/audit-records.md</sub>
- **Have each audit event state its actor type and its category explicitly, and derive its log level from its severity (info is Information, warning is Warning, critical is Critical).** The actor must not depend on how the request authenticated. Event names can share a prefix but have different categories. The log level must match the severity operators alert on. *Check:* Look for actor types taken from the authentication scheme or principal type, categories computed by splitting the event name, recorder methods that don't set an actor, or audit log levels chosen independently of severity. <sub>Identity ADR-1283; Identity docs/audit-records.md</sub>
- **Don't add a custom correlation id to audit records. Use the W3C trace and span ids of `Activity.Current`, and `HttpContext.TraceIdentifier` as the request id.** These ids let a record link straight to its traces and to the host's HTTP logs. *Check:* Look for new correlation-id fields, headers or generated ids in audit records. <sub>Identity ADR-1283</sub>
- **Add context that every audit or telemetry event needs, such as a tenant's effective type, once in the shared recorder, resolved once per entity per request. Don't pass it in from each handler.** When dozens of call sites each have to remember a value, some forget it. *Check:* Look for new audit or telemetry fields passed through individual handlers instead of being resolved centrally. <sub>Identity ADR-1289</sub>
- **Name audit events after the action on the resource, not after the owner type (for example `master_key.rotated`, not `tenant.master_key.rotated`), and carry the owner as a resource of the event.** One name then covers every owner type, and a new owner type needs no new event name. *Check:* Look for new audit event names prefixed or duplicated for each owner type. <sub>Identity ADR-1407</sub>
- **Audit an answered refresh-token retry as its own success event, distinct from rotation and from replay. Record it through one method shared by every retry path, and record nothing for a refused retry.** Operators need to tell a retry from a rotation and from a token reuse. *Check:* Check that each retry path calls the same retry-recording method and that the refusal branch records nothing. <sub>Identity ADR-1217</sub>
- **Log a distinct, named event before returning an error for a security-relevant rejection, such as a session or binding mismatch, while keeping credentials out of the message.** Without a distinct event, operators can't tell an attack attempt from an ordinary stale or invalid request. *Check:* Look for new 400/403 branches for security checks that log nothing, or that reuse a generic event. <sub>Identity outcomes of #504</sub>
- **Log each privileged principal, client or role grant that a provisioning or setup path creates, with its identifiers (such as client id and tenant id), after the save. Don't log only the primary account.** Otherwise an operator can't see in the logs that setup created a privileged client. *Check:* In setup or provisioning code, look for clients, accounts or grants created without a log message. <sub>Identity outcomes of #827</sub>
- **Don't swallow a failed cleanup of an external resource in an empty `catch`. Log at least a warning with identifying details (such as the resource id and provider), and run the cleanup on its own token with an explicit timeout rather than the caller's cancellation token.** A destroy that fails silently or is cancelled leaves an orphaned, billable resource that no record or log entry points to. *Check:* Look for `catch { }` or catches that don't log around destroy or cleanup calls, and for cleanups that pass the caller's token. <sub>Identity outcomes of #647</sub>
- **When configuration or endpoints that were validated at startup can change while the host runs, re-check them on the change token, and log each failure at `Error` with a defined event ID without stopping the host.** A later change must not stop a running host, but the operator should still see the misconfiguration in the logs, not only as failing requests. *Check:* Look for startup-only validation of reloadable or dynamic data with no change-token re-check, or a re-check that throws, stops the host, or logs without an `EventId`. <sub>Identity ADR-1433</sub>
- **When a bounded in-memory queue fed from a request path is full, drop the new item, count the drop, and log the count once per flush. Don't block the producer, throw, or log each drop.** The producing operation must never wait on the queue, and one entry per flush shows the loss without flooding the log. *Check:* Look at bounded channels or queues for a blocking write, an exception on a full queue, uncounted drops, or a log entry per item. <sub>Identity ADR-1303</sub>
- **Don't log an `OperationCanceledException` caused by the stopping token in a background service as an error or warning.** A cancelled flush at shutdown is an expected stop, not a failure. *Check:* Look at catch blocks in hosted services and background flushes for cancellation from the stopping token being logged at Warning or Error. <sub>Identity ADR-1199</sub>
- **Log a `temporarily_unavailable` protocol error at Warning with its own event ID, not at Error.** The tenant or the environment resolves this condition, and it isn't a defect in the server. *Check:* Look at the log level used for temporarily-unavailable or outage errors in exception handlers. <sub>Identity ADR-1428</sub>
- **In production code, log through source-generated `[LoggerMessage]` methods grouped in an `internal static partial class Log` of `ILogger` extension methods marked `[ExcludeFromCodeCoverage]`. Use constant message templates with named placeholders, and pass each value as its own typed parameter: never an interpolated string or a pre-built `ToString()`.** Source-generated logging is allocation-free and structured. An interpolated string is formatted even when the level is disabled, and its values are lost as structured fields. The generated code shouldn't count toward coverage. *Check:* Look for `logger.LogInformation(...)`-style calls, `$"..."` or `string.Format` arguments to log methods, `.ToString()` on log arguments, or a `Log` class without `[ExcludeFromCodeCoverage]`. *Note:* Test projects are exempt. A direct `ILogger.Log` call is a documented exception when the state keys vary per event, as in an audit logging handler that logs flattened `audit.*` state. Don't report it; only check that a `//` comment at the call cites the decision that allows it (Identity ADR-1283). <sub>Identity csharp.instructions.md; Identity csharp-production.instructions.md; Identity docs/backend-for-frontend.md; Identity outcomes of #600</sub>
- **In production code, define log event IDs as named constants in a per-package `internal static class EventIds`, as `Base + n` from a `private const int Base`, each named exactly like its `[LoggerMessage]` method. Reference the constant in `EventId = ...`, never a literal, and give each runtime package a disjoint, family-wide 1000-wide band. Don't log from `*.Abstractions` packages.** Operators key filters and alerts on stable IDs that are unique across the solution, whichever assembly emits them. Abstractions have no behavior to log. *Check:* Look for literal EventId values, constant names that don't match their method, IDs outside the package's band, overlapping bands, or logging in an abstractions package. *Applies to:* `**/*.cs` <sub>Identity csharp.instructions.md; Identity csharp-production.instructions.md</sub>
- **Never renumber assigned log event IDs, enum members or wire values to close a gap, and never renumber or reuse an ID that has shipped. Don't reserve the ID of a removed item that never shipped, either with a comment or a placeholder member; a later item may reuse it.** Log filters, alerts and parsers key on shipped IDs, and renumbering shifts every ID after the gap. A reservation protects only consumers who saw the ID, and an unshipped ID had none. *Check:* Look for diffs that change existing EventId constants or enum values, give a shipped ID to a new event, or add `// reserved` comments or placeholder members for unshipped IDs. <sub>Identity ADR-1025; Identity csharp.instructions.md; Identity csharp-production.instructions.md</sub>
- **Measure each signal once, through its owner. Don't add your own counter, histogram or span for inbound request count, latency or status, or for an outbound `HttpClient` call. Add endpoint-specific bounded tags to ASP.NET Core's `http.server.request.duration` through `IHttpMetricsTagsFeature`, and trace and measure only the package's own work, such as waits and store operations. Define a mechanism's instrument once, in the package that owns the mechanism.** ASP.NET Core and `System.Net.Http` already own these signals. Duplicate instruments double-count and drift apart. *Check:* Look for histograms, counters or `StartActivity` calls that wrap a whole endpoint handler, middleware or a single `SendAsync`, or that measure another package's mechanism. <sub>Identity ADR-1197; Identity docs/metrics.md; Identity csharp.instructions.md; Identity csharp-production.instructions.md</sub>
- **Derive the count of an audited domain outcome from its published event, not from a separate counter at the call site. Record a mechanism on a flood path, such as refused requests or counter-store calls, with a direct instrument rather than by publishing a domain event.** A parallel counter duplicates the event and drifts from it. A flood of refusals must not become a flood through the event pipeline, which is the load the limiter exists to shed. *Check:* Look for a counter incremented where an event is published for the same fact, and for rate-limit rejections or similar per-request results published as events. <sub>Identity ADR-1197; Identity csharp-production.instructions.md</sub>
- **Create a `Meter` only through an injected `IMeterFactory`, never with `new Meter(...)` or as a static field. Keep a package's instruments in one internal singleton metrics class that creates them once, and have call sites call methods on that class.** The factory scopes the meter to the host's service provider, so two hosts in one process don't share instruments and tests can read them with `MetricCollector<T>`. One owning class keeps names, units and attributes consistent. *Check:* Look for `new Meter(`, static `Meter` fields, or `CreateCounter`/`CreateHistogram`/`Add`/`Record` calls outside the package's metrics class. <sub>Identity ADR-1197; Identity ADR-1336; Identity csharp.instructions.md; Identity csharp-production.instructions.md</sub>
- **Give each package exactly one meter and, if it traces, exactly one static `ActivitySource`. Give both the package's name, and expose both names as public constants placed together.** A host can then subscribe to a package's metrics and traces, or to the whole family, with one name or wildcard. The source is static because .NET has no activity-source factory, and it costs nothing until a listener samples it. *Check:* Look for a second meter or source in one package, a name that differs from the package name or between meter and source, or a name written as an inline literal. <sub>Identity ADR-1197; Identity docs/metrics.md; Identity csharp.instructions.md; Identity csharp-production.instructions.md</sub>
- **Use the OpenTelemetry semantic-convention name for any attribute the conventions define (such as `error.type`, `http.route`, `http.response.status_code`), and name every other instrument and attribute under the family's namespace as `{product}.{area}.{name}`. Record durations as histograms with unit `s`, and give counters a curly-brace unit such as `{request}`, `{event}` or `{retry}`.** Standard names and units keep dashboards interoperable and metrics comparable. *Check:* Look for custom names for concepts the conventions define (such as `error_code`), names outside the namespace, `ms` or missing units, durations recorded on counters, or count units without braces. <sub>Identity ADR-1197; Identity docs/metrics.md; Identity csharp.instructions.md; Identity csharp-production.instructions.md</sub>
- **Make every span mirror one of the package's duration histograms: name it after the histogram without the `.duration` suffix, give it the same bounded attributes, and on failure set its status to `Error` and set `error.type`.** One vocabulary then describes both signals, so a metric spike can be traced to the matching spans. *Check:* Look for a new span with no matching histogram, a different name, missing or differently named attributes, or no `Error` status and `error.type` on failure. <sub>Identity ADR-1197; Identity docs/metrics.md</sub>
- **Route every command of a shared-state store adapter through one measuring wrapper that records its duration, adds `error.type` on an exception, and rethrows.** Every store call is then measured the same way, and failures stay visible to callers. *Check:* Look for adapter commands that call the store client directly, or a wrapper that swallows exceptions. <sub>Identity ADR-1246</sub>
- **When a change adds, renames or removes a meter, instrument, span, attribute or attribute value, update the repository's metrics catalog (name, unit, attributes and their bounded values, owner) in the same change.** The catalog is the reviewed contract that dashboards and alerts are built on, so it must match what the code emits. *Check:* Look for new or renamed instrument names, tag keys, tag values or spans with no matching edit to the catalog document (for example `docs/metrics.md`), in repositories that keep one. <sub>Identity docs/metrics.md; Identity csharp.instructions.md</sub>
- **In library packages, record telemetry only through `ILogger`, `System.Diagnostics.Metrics` and `ActivitySource`. Never register or remove logging providers, exporters or `MeterProvider`/`TracerProvider` pipelines there. Hosts export through OpenTelemetry rather than vendor-specific telemetry or APM SDKs.** Instrumentation costs nothing until a listener subscribes, and the host decides how signals are collected. Open standards let a vendor be swapped by replacing one component. *Check:* Look for `ClearProviders`, `AddConsole`, `AddProvider`, OpenTelemetry SDK or exporter references, or vendor APM packages in library projects, and for vendor SDKs used in place of OpenTelemetry in hosts. <sub>Identity ADR-1134; Identity docs/metrics.md; Identity csharp.instructions.md; Identity csharp-production.instructions.md</sub>
- **In production hosts, call `UseHttpLogging()` right after `UseRouting()`.** Endpoints opt in to body logging through metadata, and the middleware can read that metadata only after routing has run. *Check:* Check where `UseHttpLogging` sits in the middleware pipeline relative to `UseRouting`. *Applies to:* `**/*.cs` <sub>Identity csharp-production.instructions.md</sub>
- **Keep a human-readable console formatter (such as `simple`) for local development, including `launchSettings.json`, `appsettings.Development.json`, the AppHost and debug image stages. Use JSON logs only for the shipped image.** JSON logs are a contract of the shipped image only, and they are hard to read by eye during development. *Check:* Look for JSON console formatter settings added to development launch settings, development appsettings, AppHost configuration or debug Dockerfile stages. <sub>Identity ADR-1248</sub>
